criteria_changes: reports/GO2_A045_CRITERIA_CHANGES_20260924.md - what this round does and does not change against the G-A044 criteria, with the authority for each line.
promotion_reason: Both arms train at seed 43, so neither is a reward-weight change against the frozen baseline and neither may become a submission candidate whatever it scores. Two things are kept apart here. (1) What is established: no deployed file is edited - the seed is a CLI argument the deployed train.py forwards to Isaac Lab's rsl_rl train.py, and the deployed go2_task/ carries no seed at all (every earlier round passed --seed 42 down the same path). (2) What is NOT established: that technical pass-through makes the round permitted by the rules. R-6 also says participants change weights only, and 'we will not submit it' does not by itself authorise the experiment. So this field is an INTERNAL, conservative ban, not a finding that the rules forbid submitting a seed-43 policy - we have no basis for that claim either. The open reading is recorded as U2-SEED-REPLICATE-20260918 and is best closed by an organiser's answer or an explicit official basis rather than by our own reading alone. Nor do we bound the downside: if the organisers were to judge the server run itself as not permitted, whether the consequence stays inside this round is unverified - the G-A033 artifacts are preserved, but the scope of any sanction is undetermined, and a decision to run does not close the open reading.

collection.reason: Same rule as G-A044 (defect C-11: G-A043's decisive loss sat outside its 23-case stage 1). A ruler round has a second reason: there is no winner to select, so a gate that exists to schedule GPU time for winners has nothing to decide. Both arms collect all 69 in one pass.

value_derivation.role: Penalize z-axis base linear velocity using an L2 squared kernel (Isaac Lab v2.3.1, reports/evidence/go2_reward_term_roles_20260917/isaaclab_envs_mdp_rewards.py). Unchanged from G-A043 and G-A044.
value_derivation.rule: -1.5 is not chosen as a value here; it is copied from G-A043 because the question is reproduction. Choosing any other number would measure something new instead of re-measuring something old.
value_derivation.not_claimed: no gain is predicted and none may be promoted. G-A043 did not fail on G2 alone: its total gain of +2.09593/70 missed the preregistered +2.53, four non-inferiority violations were recorded (G2 scenario proxy -0.44161 and combined_yaw_right survival -0.28125/-0.28125/-0.34375 at the three evaluation seeds), and the plan screening flagged three more checks (rough_forward posture falls, push_pos_x and push_neg_x tracking). A promising stair signal and eligibility for promotion are read separately.

detectability.basis: The readout is a pair difference: this arm minus G-A045, compared with the stored G-A043 minus G-A033. The counters that moved by tens (15 cm >=1 step 4 -> 88 of 96, G2 combined_yaw_right falls 0 -> 29 of 96) are the ones read first, because a 70-point total hides two opposite movements.
detectability.expected_gain_basis: Not estimated. The measured value at this weight on the first path was +2.09593/70, below the 2.53 margin, and reproducing a number is not the same as expecting it.
detectability.seed_noise: Two seeds are not a distribution. This round produces ONE sample of training path variance and one replication attempt, so it can show that the variance is at least some size, or fail to show it is large - it cannot estimate a standard deviation, and the spec does not let a later reader treat 'D_path' as one. Every threshold in preregistered was built from evaluation resampling of seed-42 runs only (reports/GO2_SEED_SENSITIVITY.md section 0: training-seed variation measured 0 times), which is why they are lower bounds.  Two seeds are also not a cause: this pair repeats -2.0 and -1.5, not -1.75, so whatever it shows about training-path spread at those two weights, the mid-value's non-monotonic falls stay unexplained. Reward effect and training path are not exclusive either - a weight changes the trajectory, and its seed sensitivity may itself depend on the weight.

inference.rule: fact-based inference chain (2026-09-17 user instruction; MASTER section 5, AGENTS 4-9); a point-gain estimate is not required
inference.role: lin_vel_z_l2 pays -w * v_z^2 in the body frame with no sign and no direction term, so a tread's rise and a bad landing's bounce are charged alike; halving the weight halves both charges. The second thing this arm moves is the input every earlier round held fixed: the RNG seed that decides initial policy weights, environment resets and the sampling order of the whole 1000-iteration trajectory. Its role is to produce a second draw from the same training distribution.

rows.reads: the pooled posture falls of the four G6 push directions (4 cases x 3 seeds x 32 robots = 384) across the three measured values of one dial: 22 at -2.0, 66 at -1.75, 10 at -1.5. The middle value is three times worse than the weaker penalty AND three times worse than the stronger one. A dial cannot be read off that.

the same three runs, counted on the stairs instead: robots reaching at least one 15 cm step go 4 -> 39 -> 88 of 96, in order. So the dial's effect IS orderly where it acts directly, and the disorder above is somewhere else. That gap is the question this round measures rather than argues.

the midpoint run in one line: it climbed better than the baseline (62 against 43 robots two steps up the 10 cm stairs) and fell nearly twice as often on the same case (65 against 34). Its train_seed cell reads 42, like every other row in this table - that column is the one thing the project has never varied.

the frozen baseline this round re-trains at a different seed: 42.52861/70 over 69 cases, walking, at this dial's Isaac Lab value. Its replicate_of cell is empty, and so is every other row's - the ledger has a column for replicates and no replicate to put in it.

the midpoint run's total is re-scored twice with the same scorer: swap in the baseline's survival and 4.62775/70 comes back, swap in its tracking and 0.99438 goes the other way. So on these harvests the change travelled through the survival factor - an arithmetic attribution, not a cause. The interaction cell is the residual by construction, so the three parts always sum to delta_70; its size is given against two denominators (0.04% of the net change, 0.03% of the summed magnitudes) because the net-change ratio is unstable when opposite factors cancel - it is not a causal contribution and not an explanation-failure rate. G-A043 is the contrast: 79.89% against 30.75%, with its net change only 38.49% of the summed magnitudes.

contradicting.reads: against reading every fall counter as path noise: this guard counter does follow the dial. It stays at 0 for both stronger weights and only breaks at -1.5. If falls were dominated by which training path a run happened to take, this column should be noisy too, and it is not.

the weakest penalty is also the steadiest run on its feet: 17 against the baseline's 34 on the 10 cm stairs, 24 against 59 on the rough side-step, 10 against 22 on the pushes. Two of the three points therefore line up with a plain story (relax the vertical penalty, fall less), and only G-A044 sits off it. One off-trend point can be one unlucky training path - which is exactly what an untested ruler cannot tell us - but it can equally be a property of that value. This round does not assume which.

inference.singularity: Two counters read from the same three runs disagree about what the dial did. The climbed-robot counts are ordered with the weight (43 -> 62 -> 94 and 4 -> 39 -> 88); the posture-fall counts are not (34 -> 65 -> 17, 59 -> 80 -> 24, 22 -> 66 -> 10). WHERE the 70-point total moved is measured rather than argued: re-scoring G-A044 with its own tracking and the baseline's survival returns +4.62775/70, with its own survival and the baseline's tracking -0.99438, and the interaction is the residual by construction (-0.00144; reports/evidence/go2_seed_pair_20260924/SCORE_SPLIT.csv). That is an ARITHMETIC ATTRIBUTION inside a fixed scoring formula - it says the total travelled through the survival factor on these harvests, NOT that the weight change caused the falls. The residual is reported against two denominators because the first is unstable: 0.04% of the net change and 0.03% of the summed magnitudes for G-A044, against 79.89% and 30.75% for G-A043. The net-change ratio is neither a causal contribution nor an explanation-failure rate - when opposite factors cancel, the net change shrinks and the ratio blows up (G-A043's net change is only 38.49% of its summed magnitudes). What the gap between the two denominators does say is that G-A043's factors cancel heavily, which is the same fact as its scenario minimum sitting on different cases in the two arms. What no artifact can currently say is why the middle weight fell more: a weight changes the training trajectory, its seed sensitivity may depend on the weight, and the project has never repeated one reward at a second seed. Same-seed repeats do exist and came back identical (SAME_SEED_REPEAT.csv, terrain_999 0.5545 vs 0.5545 and 0.8163 vs 0.8163), so training here is deterministic at a fixed seed and the single gap is a repeat at a DIFFERENT seed.

walk.basis: removing part of a vertical penalty cannot lower the walk margin, and the same weight walked on the first path (G-A043, POLICY_LOCOMOTES). This rules out a standing policy and supports nothing else.

climb.basis: observed at this weight on the first path: pooled 15 cm >=1 step 4 -> 88 and 10 cm >=2 steps 43 -> 94 of 96 (STAIRS_CLIMB.csv). Whether it repeats on a second path is the question, so the direction is carried as the thing being tested, not as a claim.

sway.basis: the forecast sheet said down (-0.0470) and the first path measured up (+0.295513 mean proxy, rough side-step falls 59 -> 24 of 96). One arithmetic prediction already failed here, so no direction is asserted.

push.basis: same shape: the sheet predicted down and the first path came back with pooled push falls 22 -> 10 of 384, while the midpoint run came back with 66. Two runs disagree about the sign, which is why this counter is filmed and read case by case.

inference.falsified_if: Read the pair, not the absolute number alone (plan section 4-2, corrected 2026-09-24). Three questions are separated. BEHAVIOUR LEVEL: does arm B reach at least 50 of 96 robots up two or more 15 cm steps (G-A043 reached 77; G-A033 and G-A044 reached 0), or 10 and below, which says it did not appear. REWARD EFFECT: is (B - A) at the SAME seed positive and in the same direction as (G-A043 - G-A033) at seed 42 - an absolute level says nothing about the dial if A is already high. SIDE EFFECT: is the G2 combined_yaw_right posture-fall increase (B - A) in the same direction as the seed-42 move 0 -> 29 of 96. Only when BEHAVIOUR and REWARD EFFECT both hold is the stair gain called reproduced; anything else is stated as what it is, and the space between is INCONCLUSIVE. The ruler reading is equally pre-registered and equally bounded: |total(A) - 42.52861| >= 2.53 means that AT -2.0 the seed alone moved as far as the promotion margin, which narrows how far a single-seed result generalises - it does NOT retire the promotion rule, does NOT invalidate the recorded INTERNAL_GATE_FAIL verdicts of G-A042/G-A043/G-A044, and does NOT license automatic long training (nothing measured says longer training reduces this spread). Below 1.26443 the only claim is that the seed difference observed at -2.0 was small. No threshold moves after the numbers are seen, and no arm here can be promoted. This arm also carries the paired thresholds above for its own counters; the absolute 50/96 line is kept, but it now answers 'did the behaviour appear', not 'did the dial cause it'.
inference.seed_limit: Two seeds are not a distribution. This round produces ONE sample of training path variance and one replication attempt, so it can show that the variance is at least some size, or fail to show it is large - it cannot estimate a standard deviation, and the spec does not let a later reader treat 'D_path' as one. Every threshold in preregistered was built from evaluation resampling of seed-42 runs only (reports/GO2_SEED_SENSITIVITY.md section 0: training-seed variation measured 0 times), which is why they are lower bounds.  Two seeds are also not a cause: this pair repeats -2.0 and -1.5, not -1.75, so whatever it shows about training-path spread at those two weights, the mid-value's non-monotonic falls stay unexplained. Reward effect and training path are not exclusive either - a weight changes the trajectory, and its seed sensitivity may itself depend on the weight.
inference.status_reason: INFORMATION_RUN. The weight is one G-A043 already failed a screening with, so nothing here is a recommendation; and because the training seed is 43 the arm is classified training_seed and may not be promoted whatever it scores (promotion: forbidden_not_a_reward_change, open decision U2-SEED-REPLICATE-20260918). What it buys is the second half of a symmetric comparison.
inference.counterevidence_response: The adverse rows are carried, not footnoted: the relaxed end improved the fall counters at seed 42, and one guard counter moved with the dial - both make 'the midpoint spike is path noise' less certain. The design responds by repeating the value rather than interpolating from it, by pairing it with a same-seed control that carries the baseline weight, and by fixing the reproduction thresholds as counts (50/96 reproduces, 10/96 refutes) before the run. The G2 loss is filmed on both arms so a survival number cannot stand in for a behaviour.

why: The plan's goal in its own words: find out whether G-A043's stair gain and G2 loss belong to the weight or to the training path it happened to draw.
Role first (Isaac Lab formula): lin_vel_z_l2 pays -w * v_z^2 in the body frame with no direction term, so the rise a tread needs and the bounce of a bad landing cost the same.

What is measured, not argued: at this weight on the first path the pooled 15 cm >=2 step count went 0 -> 77 of 96 and combined_yaw_right posture falls went 0 -> 29 of 96, for a total of +2.09593/70 against a preregistered 2.53.

Why repeat instead of interpolate: the interpolation was tried (G-A044) and came back below both ends on the total while sitting between them on the stairs. The next thing to learn is not another value but whether these readings repeat.
Named in advance: the reproduction thresholds are numbers, not impressions - 50 of 96 reproduces the stairs, 10 or below refutes them, and the space between is INCONCLUSIVE.
